articles.title: Fantasy Football: 4 players off the waiver wire worth stashing before the NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Chris Allen suggests you add these players proactively for fantasy football before the NFL Trade Deadline.
articles.body:
Every league has that one manager. You know the type. A starter goes down on Sunday afternoon, and before you can even refresh the waiver wire, you see the backup is already on their bench. They grabbed him two weeks ago. You check the transaction log, and they've been quietly stashing handcuffs and backups all season.

It's frustrating. But they're not lucky. They're just a step ahead.

The NFL trade deadline is next Tuesday, and that's our chance to be that manager. When a veteran gets shipped out, someone on the depth chart inherits his role. By Wednesday, that player is the top waiver claim, and everyone's throwing half their FAB at him. Or we can be proactive and make the move before the NFL decides for us. Here are the players worth stashing now who could benefit when their teammates get traded.

As of this writing, Keenan Allen sits at a 59% roster rate, so he's likely sitting on someone's bench in your league. But the Colts have a couple of pockets in their schedule that make the veteran WR a worthy target in negotiations independent of what happens on Tuesday. Three of his next four matchups will be against secondaries above the league average in PPG allowed to WRs. And he has a similar setup during the fantasy playoffs (at TEN, vs. CIN). More importantly, the volume has been there for Allen even with the current personnel in Indianapolis.

So, two things from this clip of Allen from last Sunday. First, look who's throwing to him. Anthony Richardson came in for the final few drives. He attempted only three passes. Two of those throws went toward Allen. Second, check the time. It's the fourth quarter, the team is down by double digits and the 34-year-old vet is still hoarding the opportunities. He had a 42.9% target share in the fourth quarter alone. But even before Week 8, Allen was siphoning looks away from the younger talent.

Targets per Route Run: 26.7%, 1st (of all Colts pass-catchers)

Of course, the immediate concern is tying yourself to Daniel Jones. Even before the Colts started making deals, Jones ranked 30th in CPOE amongst all starters. But he hasn't had any issues getting the ball to Allen. His 80% catchable target rate sits at ninth among all WRs (min. 175 routes). Even with Downs, Allen has WR3 appeal in PPR leagues. If the Colts come out the other side of the trade deadline minus one receiver, Allen becomes a low-end WR2.

So, I don't want to overreact to a few games of Ryan Flournoy playing well. That'd be a short-sighted, results-based take. Let's look at the bigger picture. Let's start in 2026.

EPA per Target: 0.33 (Lamb), 0.42 (Pickens), 0.34 (Flournoy)

First Downs per Target: 44.6%, 45.2%, 38.6%

Explosive Play Rate: 14.9%, 21.0%, 17.8%

At 44 targets through Week 8, Flournoy's workload is less than half of Lamb's, and he's 18 looks behind Pickens. But he's making a similar impact on the offense as the primary duo. Even though most of his routes only amount to him getting his cardio workout for the day, Flournoy has generated just nine fewer first downs than Pickens. He's averaging more YAC per reception than Lamb (4.8 yards to 3.5). However, before you say this guy came out of nowhere, let's go back to 2025.

Of the 93 WRs with 250 or more routes last year, Flournoy ranked 11th in first downs per route run. Across the 12 games where all three Dallas WRs were active, Dak Prescott had the highest passer rating when targeting Flournoy. He's also opened up running lanes for his teammates downfield as a blocker . Essentially, even if Dallas doesn't move on from Pickens, Flournoy's track record has shown he should be a larger part of the passing game. That's why the past few weeks, while irritating to gamers who roster Pickens, haven't been surprising.

Week 6: 12.9% (Plays w/ 2+ TEs), 4.3% (Plays w/ 6+ OL), 1.7% (Flournoy 2WR Snap Rate)

Over the past two weeks, Dallas' play-calling has shifted to being more run-focused (-11.4% and -2.8% PROE in Weeks 7 and 8). Typically, that'd pull Flournoy off the field in favor of the Cowboys' top two. Instead, he's played more and scored his second TD of the season in the process. Flournoy is already creeping into WR3 territory as TE production in Dallas wanes. If the WR room also thins out at the deadline, Flournoy could go from a WR3 to a weekly starter overnight.

Nick Singleton/Tyjae Spears, RBs, Titans

I already relived the rollercoaster my Bengals put me through on Sunday. But at least I got to do it from Joe Burrow's perspective . However, now I need to look at it from Tennessee's side. Because it's easy to say Tony Pollard has made himself a secondary option for teams in the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes. But he didn't do it on his own.

Just rewatching Pollard's TD run , he was four yards past the line of scrimmage before somebody in orange and black got a hand on him. But the line has been slowly giving him better lanes over the past month. His rushing success rate was as low as 35.7% in Week 5, but has steadily picked up to 50+% over the past two weeks. To go with the added efficiency, Pollard's rate of carries where defenders have met him at or behind the LoS has decreased (65% in Week 6 down to 42.9%). Coupled with the fact that the Titans' PROE falls to -9.7% when they're in scoring position, if Pollard had a new home by next Wednesday, Singleton, who has an RB1 athletic profile, would be able to excel in the right matchups. But they wouldn't have to do it as rushers alone.

While Tyjae Spears was healthy, Cam Ward was targeting his RBs on 19.6% of his dropbacks. Since then, it's been down to 12.0%. Despite averaging 21.7 attempts per game as the starter, Pollard has earned only 2.3 targets a week. Spears alone was up to an 11% target rate before getting injured. Assuming a change in the backfield rotation, his utility in PPR leagues should have FLEX appeal. But before you rush to the waiver wire, be sure to check out the Titans' schedule.

Tennessee will face Jacksonville in Weeks 10 and 12. They've allowed 68.3 rushing YPG all season. In other words, there won't be a line to acquire either RB via waivers. But if you check the wire afterward, you'll likely be able to stash either on your bench for free.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes reveals comedic WWE legend slammed him "hard" on a 4-wheeler after friendly fight turned ugly
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes has made a lot of friends backstage during his lengthy tenure in WWE.
articles.body: Cody Rhodes has made a lot of friends backstage during his lengthy tenure in WWE. Moreover, Rhodes revealed that he did not shy away from having a friendly banter with them on some occasions. However, one such instance turned ugly during a friendly grappling competition between Rhodes and a WWE legend who gained popularity for his comedic antics in the company. He is none other than Santino Marella.WWE legend Santino Marella slammed Cody Rhodes hard on a 4-wheelerIn a recent interview on the Double Coverage Podcast, Cody Rhodes revealed that he and Santino Marella used to joke a lot, and there was one time when they got into a friendly grappling fight and Rhodes was able to take him down. He said, “One time we got into this little like, you know, he’s getting the Russian two-on-one and we’re starting you know when you start pushing on each other that this is going somewhere, and I got lucky and he shot in on me and I sprawled and I got lucky and I stuffed the shot and then I shot in on him and I took him down to his back and we’re in the locker room. This is no big deal. This is two points in wrestling.”However, Marella was not thrilled about being taken down. Therefore, he charged at Rhodes in anger and slammed him on the back of a four-wheeler. “It’s not — I’m not better at martial arts than Santino. But he was so angry that he picked me up over his head right as we came up, and he slammed me on a four-wheeler hard case in the back. And thank God he slammed me on that. Otherwise, I would have hit the cement”, said Rhodes.Cody Rhodes picked up a major win at WWE Crown Jewel 2026Cody Rhodes was a part of the recent WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Premium Live Event. He squared off against his former mentor Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match. The American Nightmare unleashed his most vicious side in the match to take down the dangerous and volatile Orton with no rules to stop them.In the final moments of the bout, Rhodes did the unthinkable and hit a huge punt kick on Orton to keep him down for the 10-count. With a huge win under his belt, we will have to wait and see what Rhodes does next.Also read: Former name slams WWE after John Cena Classic voting power made exclusive only to paid subscribersGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mizzou AD posts letter advocating for change in SEC replay booth transparency
articles.summary: Mizzou AD Laird Veatch posted an open letter to fans Monday, saying Missouri "requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating."
articles.body:
In an open letter to fans after several controversial rulings and officiating decisions in Mizzou's Nov. 7 loss to Texas in Columbia, Missouri athletic director Laird Veatch published an open letter to fans Monday advocating for change in the transparency of the Southeastern Conference 's replay review protocols.

The Mizzou AD also said the university "requested a formal review and response from the SEC" but, in line with conference expectations, will not publicize the contents of its conversations.

With a little more than two minutes remaining in the third quarter of Mizzou's 34-20 loss to Texas on Saturday, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was ruled to have fumbled on a third-and-10 play. The ball vaulted 14 yards past the line of scrimmage, and UT receiver Emmett Mosley V picked it up a while after it came to rest.

Because the play was ruled a fumble and not a forward pass, and because Texas picked it up, the Longhorns picked up a first down. Three plays later, Manning found wide receiver Jermaine Bishop Jr. on a third-down, 25-yard touchdown throw, sparking a game-ending 21-0 run to down the Tigers .

In his letter Monday to Mizzou fans, Veatch did not criticize any decisions made on the field or in the replay booth in Saturday's game.

The Tigers were on the wrong end of several reviewed decisions in addition to the fumble/forward pass ruling, including an overturned catch for wide receiver Cayden Lee in the third quarter, a catch from Donovan Olugbode along the sideline in the first quarter, and a potential intentional grounding ruling on Manning.

"To be clear, I don't believe in blaming or complaining about officiating," Veatch wrote in the letter. "Officials are human, and mistakes are part of the game. Coaches and players have to respond to those moments and find ways to overcome adversity. That is why I greatly respect and appreciate how Coach Drinkwitz handled his postgame response with the media and his team."

Instead, Mizzou, its athletic director and university president are asking for the SEC to consider making a change that has become common in other conferences: Providing live audio or video from its replay booth.

"After the game Saturday, we requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating," Veatch wrote. "Consistent with SEC expectations, we will not make those conversations or responses public, other than that we have not received anything inconsistent with what the conference has already shared publicly.

"This experience has reinforced my belief that our lack of transparency in the replay booth, particularly when other conferences have taken steps to provide it, allows for an environment of speculation and mistrust. Together with President Choi, we will be strong advocates for that change within the SEC this offseason."

The SEC is the only Power conference that does not air live video or audio from its replay booth. The Big Ten and Big 12 began doing so this season, and the ACC began airing conversations about officiating decisions in 2025.

The SEC also does not allow for a designated pool reporter to ask questions to officials after controversial decisions, which is common in professional leagues.

When reached for comment by the Columbia Daily Tribune on Saturday after the game, the SEC provided the following statement on the fumble ruling.

"The ruling on the field was a fumble," an SEC official wrote in an e-mail to the Tribune. "In replay review it was determined there was not clear and obvious video evidence that he had firm control of the ball when the hand intentionally started forward in order to overturn the call."

Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz and MU's players did not criticize the officials or any decisions in postgame media availability.

"If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that because I'm not going to blame the officials," Drinkwitz said Saturday. "That'd be disrespectful to Coach Sark and his team."

Veatch complimented Drinkwitz for how he handled his postgame comments in the open letter to fans.

Missouri (6-3, 3-3 SEC) has three games left in the regular season, beginning with a trip to face newly No. 1-ranked Georgia on Saturday, Nov. 14 in Athens, Georgia.

The Tigers will then face Kentucky and Oklahoma in back-to-back weeks on Faurot Field to finish the regular season.

"It's OK to acknowledge that Saturday hurt," Veatch wrote. "In fact, our collective frustration and disappointment is evidence of how high our program expectations have elevated.

"Now let's turn our attention to Georgia and the opportunities ahead, including two huge home games against Kentucky and Oklahoma. Our coaches and players deserve our support, and I know this fan base will continue to show up with the passion and pride that make Saturdays in CoMo so special."

articles.title: Lakers Star Hits Injury Report as Another Star Returns to Action
articles.summary: Luka Doncic returns to action for the Lakers against the Hawks on Monday, but Austin Reaves hits the injury report as questionable and Quentin Grimes is out....
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are facing off with the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, and while they're getting one star guard back, the other may be out of action.

Luka Doncic missed Sunday's win over the Detroit Pistons with a back issue , but he'll be in action on Monday.

He might be without fellow guard Austin Reaves, though, as he's been listed as questionable on the team's injury report.

Why is Austin Reaves questionable for Monday's Lakers game?

Reaves is dealing with an illness, leading to his questionable status for Monday's game at the Hawks, as reported by Khobi Price of the California Post .

Reaves scored 43 on Sunday in Doncic's absence , and if he's out or limited on Monday, Doncic will likely have to pick up the slack, but that shouldn't be a problem for the Slovenian superstar.

He's averaging more than 40 points per game thus far this season, a truly incredible rate of scoring that could help him in his pursuit of his first MVP award.

It's possible that Doncic could score 50 points again, a level he's already reached twice this season on Oct. 25 against the Utah Jazz and on Nov. 6 against the Portland Trail Blazers.

This kind of scoring pace has only been seen once before in the last 40 years, the team noted on social media .

Through his first eight games, Doncic scored more than 300 points, and the only other player to ever do that was Michael Jordan in the 1988-89 season.

Even if Reaves is good to play with his questionable status, the Lakers will be down a guard.

Quentin Grimes is out with a right finger sprain, Price reports.

Grimes "banged his finger," coach JJ Redick said, and while X-rays showed no break, he'll need some time to recover.

With Grimes and possibly Reaves out as well, Monday is shaping up to be another Luka Doncic showcase.

Do you think Luka Doncic will score 50 points again against the Hawks?

articles.title: Antetokounmpo Says Heat Players Don’t Trust Each Other
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo admits the team lacks trust after a blowout loss. Klay Thompson and Erik Spoelstra weigh in on the rocky start.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo said the Miami Heat do not trust one another after a Monday loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. Miami surrendered 138 points in the defeat, falling to 2-5. The Heat have since improved to 4-6, but their early struggles have exposed serious problems on defense. The five-time All-Star made the comment during a rough start where Miami has been outscored by 53 points through 10 games. It is a stark admission from a player who joined the team in July after a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Heat defense has been terrible despite having elite defenders on the roster. With six All-Defensive team selections to his credit, Center Bam Adebayo joins Antetokounmpo, a former Defensive Player of the Year. Yet the unit ranks 25th in the league. Klay Thompson, who played 13 minutes in the loss, told ESPN that the team needs to stay present. "It's important for all of us to stay present and not look too far ahead in the season," Thompson told ESPN. He added that the group must think week to week rather than focus on the postseason.

Heat coach Erik Spoelstra dismissed the idea that the team just needs more time to gel. "It can't just be on paper, and it can't just be reputation," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. He insisted that the culture must be backed by real actions. Spoelstra scoffed at the suggestion that the team simply needed time to fix these issues when asked. "I don't know, but we don't want to use that as an excuse," he said. "The league's not waiting."

Giannis and Klay Joined a Messy Situation

Klay Thompson gave up millions in contract value to join Miami this summer. He left the Dallas Mavericks to play alongside Antetokounmpo, whom he believes can still lead a great team. Thompson said he loves the organization's intensity and called the move a full-circle moment, since his dad played for Pat Riley. "That Heat culture is real," Thompson said. However, the 4-6 record indicates the team must improve significantly before achieving greatness or securing a playoff spot.

articles.title: Ryan Hopkins wins Big Ten freshman of the week honor after first career start
articles.summary: The Badgers quarterback had a strong start this weekend.
articles.body:
Wisconsin Badgers true freshman Ryan Hopkins shone in his first start, throwing for 241 yards and three touchdowns in the team's 31-10 win over the Rutgers Scarlet Knights.

That caught the eyes of Badgers fans, who were impressed by the freshman and began to ask why Hopkins hadn't been playing even earlier in the season. Well, the performance also caught the eye of the Big Ten, as Hopkins was named the Big Ten Freshman of the Week on Monday.

Here's what the Big Ten said in their statement on Monday about Hopkins's selection.

The true freshman quarterback made his first career start on Saturday in Wisconsin's 31-10 win vs. Rutgers

Recorded 241 yards and three scores on 18-of-24 passing, with his 241 passing yards tying for the third most for a Badger freshman in their debut since 1990

Hopkins' three passing touchdowns were the most by any freshman in the nation this week and his 200.6 passer rating led all FBS freshmen in week 10 action

Threw scores of 66, 21 and 11 yards, all to different Badger receivers, with eight different Badgers catching passes in the win

Last Wisconsin Freshman of the Week: Mason Posa (Nov. 10, 2025)

UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach won Offensive Player of the Week, Michigan State cornerback NihJay Burt won Defensive Player of the Week, and Michigan State kicker Liam Boyd won Special Teams Player of the Week.

Hopkins is the third Badger to win a weekly award this week. Colton Joseph was the Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week back in Week 5 during the team's win over Michigan State, and Sebastian Cheeks won Defensive Player of the Week two weeks ago.

He's set to start the rest of the way for the Badgers and will look to build on his performance this weekend against the Maryland Terrapins.

articles.title: ESPN grades Jaguars-Saints trade for Davon Godchaux
articles.summary: What grade did the Jacksonville Jaguars receive for their role in the Davon Godchaux trade with the New Orleans Saints?
articles.body:
What grade did the Jacksonville Jaguars receive for their role in the Davon Godchaux trade with the New Orleans Saints ?

According to Jordan Schultz , the Jaguars are sending a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Saints for Godchaux. The selection could become a 2027 sixth-round pick if the Jaguars acquire one via the comp pick formula or another trade.

Listed at 6-3, 330 pounds, Godchaux can help fill that run-stuffing, nose tackle role for the Jaguars, who are without DaVon Hamilton for the remainder of the season due to a quad injury.

Godchaux's impact won't always show up on the stat sheet, but his ability to take on blocks and occupy space can open up opportunities for others.

ESPN grades Jaguars-Saints Davon Godchaux trade

The Jaguars earned a B- for this trade from ESPN, while the Saints were given a B.

"In his 10th season in the league, Godchaux was playing just under 20 snaps per game for the Saints. His run stop win rate ranked in the 65th percentile among interior defenders this season, though he had struggled in the category the prior two years. Godchaux has a $1.3 million salary and is in the last year of his contract."

This was a trade that will give the Jaguars a needed boost, but also one that likely comes with a lower ceiling, hence ESPN's modest grade.

articles.title: Nate Oats announces Aden Holloway will return from suspension for Oakland game
articles.summary: The Alabama Crimson Tide are looking to start of the 2026-27 season at 3-0 as they face off against the visiting Oakland Golden Grizzlies on Monday evening,...
articles.body:
The Alabama Crimson Tide are looking to start of the 2026-27 season at 3-0 as they face off against the visiting Oakland Golden Grizzlies on Monday evening, and they'll have a boost in the lineup as well. Alabama head coach Nate Oats acknowledged that star guard Aden Holloway would return to the lineup following a suspension and would play starters minutes, as per Jon Rothstein of 247Sports.

Aden Holloway was serving a suspension by the university following drug related charges last season, while he had remained on the Alabama roster. The incident occurred during March of last season, right before the start of the NCAA Tournament, and Holloway missed the Crimson Tide's run to the Sweet 16 . He was suspended for five games, which included the three exhibition games that Alabama played.

Considered a five-star recruit coming out of high school, Holloway was in the midst of a breakout seasons with Alabama last year. He appeared in 28 games, including 27 starts, at a little over 28 minutes per game. As a junior, he averaged 16.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists with splits of 48.1 percent shooting from the field, 43.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 86.4 percent shooting from the free-throw line.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Holloway is now in his senior year of college basketball eligibility after spending the past two seasons at Alabama. He initially began his college career at Auburn where he played his freshman year before entering the transfer portal.

The Crimson Tide are in the program's eighth season with Nate Oats at the helm as head coach. The team is currently ranked No. 20 in the men's college basketball AP top-20 poll.

articles.title: Dan Quinn discusses Commanders’ downfall vs. Rams, complete-game quest
articles.summary: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn discussed why Washington lost to the Rams and the fixes available moving forward
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders lost another game on Sunday, this one a 20-13 result against the Los Angeles Rams. Their record sits at 2-5-1 , putting their season on the brink if it isn't over already.

The 24-hour rule doesn't even apply here despite extreme frustration with Washington's inability to get out of it's own way. Why?

A defining matchup with the New York Giants is on the immediate horizon, scheduled for primetime on Thursday night football .

While Quinn preached the fact that the Commanders must move on quickly, the Commanders head coach also addressed some missteps against the Rams in his Monday virtual press conference.

Quinn backed offensive coordinator David Blough , whose play calling has taken sharp criticism from the fan base. He discussed the need for more consistent execution but also said there's a need for better at the end of games.

Quinn also outlined his communication routines with owner Josh Harris, the need for improvement in the. run game and why Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett got loose and wrecked Sunday's game.

articles.title: ESPN gives FSU basketball little room for error against Florida
articles.summary: ESPN’s Matchup Predictor gives Florida State just a 13.8% chance to beat No. 1 Florida at the Tucker Center.
articles.body:
Florida State basketball is off to a 2-0 start under Luke Loucks, but ESPN does not like the Seminoles' chances in their first major test of the season.

According to ESPN's Matchup Predictor , FSU has just a 13.8% chance to beat No. 1 Florida Gators on Tuesday night at the Donald L. Tucker Center. The Gators are given an 86.2% chance to win despite playing on the road.

The projection sets up a sharp contrast with Florida State's strong start. The Seminoles have yet to trail through two games, opening with a 113-69 win over the Florida A&M Rattlers before beating the Troy Trojans 91-68 in their home opener. FSU is averaging 102.0 points per game and has out-rebounded its first two opponents 93-50.

Sebastian Rancik has led the offense at 21.5 points per game, while freshman center Marcis Ponder has recorded a double-double in each of his first two college games. Shon Abaev is also averaging six assists per game with just one turnover through the opening week.

Florida represents a much different challenge.

The Gators entered the season ranked No. 1 in both the AP and US LBM Coaches polls and are also 2-0. Florida opened with a 77-67 win over No. 14 Miami before cruising past Jacksonville 88-57. The Gators have shot 43.1% from 3-point range and are averaging 48 rebounds per game.

Florida has also won the last five meetings in the rivalry, including a 78-76 victory over FSU last season. The Gators lead the all-time series 49-28.

Still, Tuesday offers Loucks and the Seminoles an early opportunity to change the perception around this team. FSU has looked dominant through two games, and now it gets a chance to test that start against the top-ranked team in the country.

Florida State and Florida tip off at 6 p.m. ET Tuesday at the Tucker Center, with the game airing on ESPN2.

articles.title: Spurs rule out Devin Vassell for Monday night's game at Phoenix
articles.summary: It will be the first game this season without the seventh-year forward, who is averaging 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists.
articles.body:
PHOENIX - The red-hot Spurs will be without Devin Vassell when they face the Phoenix Suns on Monday night.

The Spurs, who have won eight games in a row, downgraded the starting forward from questionable to out because of left adductor tightness after shootaround at the Mortgage Matchup Center.

It's unclear when Vassell suffered the injury.

The seventh-year pro played 21 minutes in the Spurs' 125-103 pounding of Portland on Saturday night, finishing with 15 points on 4 of 8 from the field and 2 of 4 from 3-point range. He also had three assists, two rebounds and two steals.

Through 10 games this season, Vassell is averaging 30.0 minutes, 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.7 steals while shooting 35.6% from beyond the arc on 3.4 attempts and a team-high 96.2% from the free-throw line.

Forward Tobias Harris was also ruled out of Monday's game. The 16th-year player has yet to make his debut with the Spurs after suffering a calf injury in the first week of training camp.

The Spurs signed Harris to a two-year deal worth $31 million in the offseason.
